Rarity.rationale: StoneCracker.cs:16 is RelicRarity.Uncommon. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-pool): Uncommon in the transcribed grab bag, so it is obtainable from any relic reward with no event required -- binding rule 6's relic-side leg.

AfterRoomEntered.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and N1 per binding rule 4. The candidate FILTER and the count are right, but the port hands StableShuffle the wrong pile ORIENTATION and the wrong SORT KEY, so the wrong two cards are upgraded (G1, LIVE); and the hook site is one dispatch later than C#'s (G2).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): StableShuffle is fed the draw pile BACKWARDS and sorted on the lowercase slug, so a different pair of draw-pile cards is upgraded -- 6 of 8 seeds diverge on the plain starting deck
guards.issue: MECHANISM. StoneCracker.cs:25-27 is `PileType.Draw.GetPile(Owner).Cards.Where(c => c.IsUpgradable).ToList().StableShuffle(RunState.Rng.CombatCardSelection).Take(Cards.IntValue)`. ListExtensions.StableShuffle (ListExtensions.cs:22-31) first `List.Sort()`s -- CardModel.CompareTo (CardModel.cs:2242-2264) which delegates to AbstractModel.CompareTo's `Id.CompareTo(other.Id)` (AbstractModel.cs:87-98) and then tiebreaks on CurrentUpgradeLevel -- and THEN runs UnstableShuffle, an order-DEPENDENT Fisher-Yates (ListExtensions.cs:33-45 documents exactly that: 'the result is dependent on the initial order of the list'). Two inputs to that sort are wrong in the port, and the sim's own code already documents both. (a) ORIENTATION: player.py:264-266 states 'the game stores the pile top-at-index-0 but the sim draws off the END of the list' and _shuffle_draw_pile reverses after every parity shuffle to reproduce the game's draw order; stone_cracker.py:18 iterates `self.player.draw_pile` as-is, i.e. bottom-first, and cards that COMPARE EQUAL keep their incoming order under both List.Sort and Python's sort -- and a starting deck is nothing but equal-comparing cards (5 Strikes, 4 Defends). (b) KEY: player.py:23-34's `_compare_to_key` is `(card.id.upper(), card.upgrade_level)` and its docstring spells out why -- ModelId.cs compares the game's UPPERCASE entry ORDINALLY, where `_` (0x5F) sorts AFTER the uppercase letters but BEFORE the lowercase ones -- while stone_cracker.py:29 keys on `(c.id, c.upgrade_level)`, the lowercase slug. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-cracker), A/B-ing the shipped port against a StoneCracker.cs-faithful variant on the same seed and the same CombatCardSelection stream: 6 of 8 seeds produce a DIFFERENT observable opening hand and draw pile. Seed 89U21BV1TZ -- port hand ['strike','defend','strike','defend','strike'], game hand ['strike+','defend','strike','defend+','strike']: the port upgraded two cards that stayed in the draw pile and the game upgraded two that were dealt. Seed 933T39V18D -- port ['strike+',...] vs game [...] with the pluses in the pile instead. Seed QRWC12345X, TZEK9876HJ, AAAA111111, DJDC1X0MHK likewise. REACHABILITY (LIVE, both sides ported, nothing exotic needed): the relic is Uncommon in the grab bag (executed b15-pool) and the divergence appears on the DEFAULT Ironclad starting deck with no other content, in the parity path the conformance runner uses. The lowercase-key half is independently reachable too -- the same probe finds three ported adjacent id pairs the two keys order oppositely: blood_wall/bloodletting, byrd_swoop/byrdonis_egg, jack_of_all_trades/jackpot. FIX NOTE: the sim already has the correct key as `player._compare_to_key`; the call needs it plus `reversed(self.player.draw_pile)`. The sibling site relics/fragrant_mushroom.py:33-37 copies the same lowercase key (over the DECK, not a pile, so only the key half applies there) -- it is not in this batch, so no verdict is issued for it; reported in .superpowers/sdd/relic-batch-15-lessons.md. Rule 7: leans on player.py, sts2_rl/actmap.py's stable_shuffle and relics/fragrant_mushroom.py, none hashed here.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): the C# hook is AfterRoomEntered, which runs one full dispatch BEFORE Hook.BeforeCombatStart; the port uses on_combat_start
guards.issue: POOL-WIDE SHAPE (executed census, py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-censuses): TWELVE ported relics whose C# combat effect hangs off `AfterRoomEntered` with a `room is CombatRoom` test are mapped onto the sim's on_combat_start -- bronze_scales, ember_tea, ghost_seed, girya, gorget, oddly_smooth_stone, philosophers_stone, red_skull, stone_cracker, sword_of_jade, throwing_axe, vajra -- and the sim's on_combat_start IS Hook.BeforeCombatStart, which is ONE DISPATCH LATER: CombatRoom.cs:228 fires Hook.AfterRoomEntered right after CombatManager.SetUpCombat (CombatManager.cs:350-376, which has already cloned and shuffled the draw pile via Player.PopulateCombatState, Player.cs:802-811), and only then does AfterCombatRoomLoaded -> StartCombatInternal reach Hook.BeforeCombatStart (CombatManager.cs:380-403). So C# guarantees that EVERY AfterRoomEntered relic acts before EVERY BeforeCombatStart relic, and the sim flattens both groups into one listener walk in relic-list order. This is PROMPT.md bug class 20 (right hook, wrong SITE) crossed with class 25 (a two-pass ordering guarantee destroyed by a single walk). AT THIS SITE the candidate set is unaffected -- executed (CombatManager.cs:350-366) SetUpCombat has already populated and shuffled the draw pile, so the pile Stone Cracker reads is the same at both points. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, and the census is executed rather than asserted, py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-censuses plus the on_combat_start body scan reported in the batch-15 lessons file): of the sim's 23 on_combat_start implementers, only two touch the draw pile -- this relic (AfterRoomEntered side) and relics/tea_of_discourtesy.py:27-40 (BeforeCombatStart side, TeaOfDiscourtesy.cs:56-64, shuffles 2 Dazed in at random positions) -- and their interaction is provably order-free: Dazed has max_upgrade_level 0 so it never joins Stone Cracker's candidate list, Stone Cracker never changes the pile's SIZE so it cannot move Tea's `Rng.Shuffle.NextInt(Cards.Count + 1)` insert positions, and the two draw from DIFFERENT streams (CombatCardSelection vs Shuffle), so neither can shift the other's stream position either. No two combat-start relics on opposite sides of the collapse share an RNG stream at all. What makes it live: porting any BeforeCombatStart relic or power that adds/removes/upgrades draw-pile cards, or one that draws from CombatCardSelection at combat start.

guards.what: N1: `Where(c => c.IsUpgradable)` (StoneCracker.cs:25) and CardCmd.Upgrade's own IsUpgradable filter -- PROMPT.md bug class 14
guards.rationale: The sim's Card.upgrade() (cards/base.py:146-147) is a bare `upgrade_level += 1` with no guard, so every caller must pre-filter, and 35 of 203 ported cards have max_upgrade_level 0. This port DOES pre-filter: stone_cracker.py:18 builds `upgradable = [c for c in ... if c.is_upgradable]`, and Card.is_upgradable (cards/base.py:168-170) is `upgrade_level < max_upgrade_level`, exactly CardModel.IsUpgradable (CardModel.cs:785-789). Mechanically confirmed: `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-upgrade` lists stone_cracker in its 'guarded (for contrast)' bucket, and sweep D in .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md records that an earlier 3-line-window version of that sweep FALSE-FLAGGED this relic before it was made AST-scoped. So the sweep's clearance here is confirmed on the merits, not inherited. Rule 7: cards/base.py and audit/tools/relic_probes.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: `min(self.CARDS, len(upgradable))` (stone_cracker.py:19) vs C#'s `.Take(2)` on a possibly shorter list
guards.rationale: LINQ Take(n) yields min(n, count) elements without error, and the sim's explicit min reproduces that. Checked because the legacy arm uses random.sample, which RAISES when count exceeds the population -- so the clamp is load-bearing for a deck of one upgradable card, and it is present. CardsVar(2) read as IntValue (StoneCracker.cs:18, 26) has no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so CARDS = 2 is the pinned non-ascension value.

guards.what: N3: the upgrade is applied to COMBAT cards, so it must not persist into the run deck
guards.rationale: Verified on both sides because the relic's text says 'for the rest of the combat' and a permanent upgrade would be a deck-parity failure. C#: Player.PopulateCombatState CLONES every deck card into the draw pile and records DeckVersion (Player.cs:802-811), so CardCmd.Upgrade mutates the clone. Sim: CombatState deep-copies the run deck and keeps the id(clone) -> origin map `deck_card_origins` (combat.py:185-190; RunState.create_combat populates it), and RunState.finish_combat syncs only HP/max-HP/potions/gold plus the Thieving-Hopper removal back to the run (run.py:1170-1207) -- never upgrade levels. Both sides therefore drop the upgrade at combat end. Rule 7: combat.py, run.py and Player.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N4: the LEGACY arm's `self.combat._rng.sample(upgradable, count)` (stone_cracker.py:32) instead of the CombatCardSelection stream
guards.rationale: The port branches on `crng.is_parity` (stone_cracker.py:21) and uses the shared legacy random.Random in the non-parity arm. This is the repo's established two-mode contract, stated in combat_rng.py:1-11 -- legacy mode keeps RL training/eval sequences byte-for-byte unchanged and only string-seeded parity runs reproduce the game -- and the same shape appears at relics/fragrant_mushroom.py:31-38. It is NOT PROMPT.md bug class 16's silent fallback: the stream is named and consumed in the arm that claims parity. Verdicted deliberate-divergence rather than gap because the divergent thing is which of the sim's two declared execution modes is running, and no parity comparison ever observes the legacy arm. G1 is the defect INSIDE the parity arm and is filed separately.
